name: Quick and Easy Chocolate Chip Cookies | BraveTart

ingredients.name: all purpose flour, such as Gold Medal
kosher salt, plus more for sprinkling

instructions.primary_message: Let the unsalted butter soften slightly but keep it cool and bring it to 65°F. Keep the egg cold until you use it.

Make the Dough: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat to 180°C (350°F). Set aside a handful of chopped chocolate (about 57 g; 55g) and place the remainder in a medium bowl. Sift flour on top and toss together. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, vanilla, salt, baking soda, baking powder, and nutmeg in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment. Mix on low to moisten, then increase to medium and beat until light and fluffy, about 5 minutes. With mixer running, add egg and continue beating only until smooth. Reduce speed to low, add flour/chocolate all at once, and mix to form a stiff dough.

Portion the Dough: Divide in 2-tablespoon portions (about 43 g or 40g each) and round each one into a smooth ball. (If you like, portioned dough can be refrigerated in a heavy-duty zipper-lock bag up to 1 week, or frozen 6 months. Stand at room temperature until quite soft, about 21°C or 21°C, and proceed as directed.)

To Bake: Arrange portions on a parchment-lined half sheet pan, leaving 5 cm between cookies to account for spread. Garnish each with reserved chocolate and a pinch of kosher salt. Bake until puffed and pale gold around the edges but steamy in the middle, about 15 minutes. For crunchy cookies, continue baking until golden, 3 to 5 minutes more. Cool directly on baking sheet until crumb is set, about 5 minutes. Enjoy warm or store in an airtight container up to 2 days at room temperature.

description: Chewy chocolate chip cookies with just-crisp edges, loaded with melted chopped bar chocolate for better flavor than commercial chips.
notes:
Notes: With kitchen temperatures above 23°C, start by refrigerating the mixing bowl and dry ingredients until cooled to 21°C. At elevated temperatures, these ingredients and equipment can act as a heat source to the butter, warming the dough and causing excessive spread in the oven.

Make-ahead and storage: The portioned dough can be refrigerated in a heavy-duty zipper-lock bag up to 1 week, or frozen 6 months. Stand at room temperature until quite soft, about 21°C or 21°C, and proceed as directed. Though these chocolate chip cookies are best enjoyed warm, they can be kept for up to 2 days in an airtight container at room temperature.
author: Stella Parks
